paper_metadata.title: Novel Cast Ni-Based Superalloys with Superb Weldability and Mechanical Properties Screened by a Multiperformance-Oriented Criterion

evidence.quote: Herein, innovative cast Ni-based superalloys that not only withstand temperatures up to 800 °C but also offer superior weldability, robust tensile strength at both room and elevated temperatures, and a reduced density are introduced.

To bridge the gap in the service temperature of IN718 alloy, cast IN939 polycrystalline alloy strengthened by a high fraction of γ 0(Ni3Al) precipitates was developed, which can be used for the hot sections of aeroengines served at ≈800 °C.
To illustrate the applicability of this scheme, the heritage alloy IN939 was also prepared with the same processing parameters for comparison.

The as-cast cylindrical bars of the selected alloys with 75 mm length and 13 mm diameter were prepared using investment casting at the Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials. The pouring temperature and mold shell temperature were 1400 and 930 °C, respectively.
High-temperature solution treatments for the selected alloys were performed at 1160 °C for 4 h, followed by air cooling.

Then, a two-stage aging treatment, involving the first treatment at 1080 °C for 4 h followed by air cooling and the second treatment at 845 °C for 20 h followed by air cooling, was conducted to obtain fine spherical γ 0 precipitates.
